{{Top}}
[[File:HologramProjectionPod-NEGWT.png|thumb|200px|A [[HoloNet transceiver/Legends|hologram projection pod]]]]
A '''holoprojector'''&mdash;also known as a '''holo-projector''', '''holojector''', '''hologram projector''', '''holograph projector''',<ref name="SWS">''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]''</ref> '''holoproj''', and ''''proj'''<ref name="DS">[[Death Star (novel)|''Death Star'']]</ref>&mdash;was a device that could record, transmit and receive [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]] images. Traditionally, these images were used for communication, but some holoprojectors, known as '''holo-emitters''', were also designed as tools for entertainment and academic purposes. Most [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droids]] were outfitted with a holoprojector.

Holoprojectors projected an organized arrangement of light to create a 3-D replica of the subject. These '''holograms''' were used for communication, information displays, and entertainment. Most holoprojectors were equipped with sound so that the user could hear the subject talk in perfect sync.

==Description==
[[File:Namman_Cha_SWGTCG_by_Chris_Dien.jpg|thumb|left|180px|[[Namman Cha]] using a handheld holoprojector]]
Holoprojectors could project real-time or pre-recorded three-dimensional images, which could even be transferred through a [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]] connection.<ref name="SWCVD">''[[Star Wars: The Complete Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> Sound capability typically doubled the cost of a handheld holoprojector. The device had a limited storage capacity, but this could be expanded by connecting it to a [[Holorecorder/Legends|holorecorder]]. A personal holoprojector weighed roughly half a [[Kilogram/Legends|kilogram]], and from [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] to [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]], it cost around 1,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]].<ref name="RPG-Core">''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game Core Rulebook]]''</ref>

Miniaturized holoprojectors could be installed inside [[Datapad/Legends|datapads]] and [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droids]],<ref name="EGWT">''[[The Essential Guide to Weapons and Technology]]''</ref> such as the [[R2-series astromech droid/Legends|R2-series]].<ref name="EGTD">''[[The Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref>

Some holo-emitters were designed to project a [[holopet]]. The holo-emitter would read data from an inserted [[holo-pet data cube]] that contained the characteristics of unique holopets.<ref name="SWG">{{GalaxiesNGE}}</ref>

==History==
[[File:Jedi_Temple_Tython_holoprojectors-Full.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Holoprojectors in the [[Jedi Temple (Tython)/Legends|Jedi Temple]] on [[Tython/Legends|Tython]]]]
The [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] maintained a large holoprojector in his [[Chancellor's Suite/Legends|office]] in the [[Republic Executive Building/Legends|Republic Executive Building]], from which he could view reports from [[Senator/Legends|Senators]], Republic agents and [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]. Succeeding galactic governments, from the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] to the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]], made use of holoprojectors. In particular, the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] used these projectors to view holographic recordings that were produced by cameras installed on their [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]]. They would study these recordings for tactical purposes.
